title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Commissioning Affidavits
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client emails a signed affidavit to their paralegal and asks the paralegal to commission it. The paralegal was not present physically or virtually when the client signed the document. Is it ethical for the paralegal to sign as a commissioner?
options: Yes, provided the paralegal recognizes the client's signature.
Yes, if the client later confirms over the phone that they signed it.
No, an affidavit must be sworn or affirmed in the physical or valid virtual presence of the commissioner.
No, paralegals do not have the authority to commission affidavits in Ontario.
questions.explain: Under the Commissioners for Taking Affidavits Act and LSO Rules, a commissioner must administer an oath or affirmation with the deponent physically present (or virtually present following strict regulatory protocols for remote commissioning). Backdating or commissioning a pre-signed document without administering the oath/affirmation is professional misconduct.
